pageCache.pageTitle: Award Winning Private School Sussex | Westbourne House School
pageCache.text:
Think.Thrive.Trailblaze.
Join us on 3 October: meet school leaders, take a tour with pupils and see our outstanding facilities.
You will find that there is no better way to discover the spirit of Westbourne House than through the eyes of our pupils. They will walk you through their world: favourite lessons, lunchtime laughter, leadership roles, hobbies and everything in between. Along the way, you will also see Years 4–6 immersed in their optional Saturday activities, whether that’s kayaking on the lake, experimenting in science or creating in the art studio.
Click to learn more.
Welcome to Westbourne House School - An Award Winning Private School in Sussex
Westbourne House School is an independent co-educational day and boarding school for children aged 2-13 in Chichester, West Sussex.
"We encourage our pupils to take risks, see mistakes as opportunities and then go further than they ever thought possible." Guy Musson, Headmaster
At Westbourne House, children dive into ideas and ask thoughtful questions.
Our specialist teachers guide them and help their curiosity build exciting momentum.
This is a kind, happy place where imagination roams, friendship grows and mistakes are simply part of the adventure.
By the time our pupils look ahead to senior school, they are ready, confident and excited to blaze their own trail.
"Westbourne House is a very special place for children to grow up. We are a non-selective school and we are proud to give each and every pupil an outstanding start to their education. As parents, you will also have the whole-hearted support and commitment of me and my team, from your first day to your last," said Mr Musson, Headmaster
Read all of Mr Musson's welcome here.
What defines Westbourne House? The joyful opportunities, the culture of kindness and of encouraging children to grasp new possibilities with confidence.
Think. Thrive. Trailblaze.
The mission of our school is not to fast-track excellence, but to preserve that spark, the inner drive, that pushes a child to explore, fail, try again, and stay endlessly curious about the world.
Every lesson invites curiosity - puzzling through a problem, debating a viewpoint or discovering new connections -helping your child grow into a thoughtful, confident and independent thinker.
You’ll watch your child take risks, try new things and keep going when it’s tricky, learning more about themselves with every challenge.
From creative projects and public speaking competitions to collaborative challenges, your child will practise life skills every day.
Our pupils don't just move on to brilliant senior schools, they move up, ready to make their mark on the world.
At our Nursery in Chichester, we champion the wonder, surprise and delight of enquiry-led learning and exploration. Each child is encouraged, supported and loved every step of the way.
"Luca receives the warmest of welcomes every day, he rushes in to nursery with eager eyes excitedly awaiting the day’s adventure!"
— Nicola, Westbourne House Parent
Step inside our magic haven for learning and adventure. We mould each child’s educational experience to bring light into their eyes.
“The Pre-Prep has the most wonderful, energetic, caring and lively feel to it. The opportunities and facilities are immense.”
— Charlie, Westbourne House parent
We encourage pupils to take intellectual risks and embrace a “brave, not perfect” ethos, giving them the confidence to question, explore and challenge ideas.
"Westbourne House is ambitious for each and every pupil."
— Harriet, Westbourne House Parent
Explore what makes our Prep school such an inspiring place.
Westbourne House School is the winner of a national award – the Alice Rose Award - in the Talk Education Awards for Innovation in Education.
The judges were looking for a school where "children are allowed to be children, one that supports growth and learning but allows them to climb trees and get muddy knees, where confident, nurtured, happy children enjoy their childhood. A true home-from-home."
It is a very special accolade which has brought us immense pride.
Trailblaze.

pageCache.text:
Music
A thrilling hive of activity, the Music School is a special place to be at whatever time of day you happen to visit. A ‘music for all’ philosophy ensures that every child benefits from specialist tuition and experiences the wonderful feeling of collective music making, whilst also having the opportunity to excel in whichever instruments they choose.
Our four music staff are experts in their field, and are joined by a team of over twenty peripatetic teachers who deliver one-to-one lessons. Around 75% of children learn at least one instrument, with many learning two or more. Regular concerts provide children with the opportunity to display their talents.
Select an option below
Our pupils are taught by a music specialist from their very earliest days at school. Singing is an integral part of the Pre-Prep with the children from Nursery through to Year 2 coming together for a weekly singing assembly.
We take part in the National ‘Sing Up’ Day to share the importance of singing on well-being and community.
Our Nursery children experiment with instruments, rhythms and dynamics as well as learning fun songs in their weekly lesson. As the children progress in to Reception they continue to develop their skills in the elements of music through a weekly music and movement lesson.
In Year 1 the children deepen their understanding of rhythm and pitch with the introduction of simple notation and rhythm games. They also listen to and appraise pieces of classical music in order to consolidate their knowledge of the elements of music.
We are very proud of our ‘Pre Prep Live’ sessions which bring great joy and excitement to the Year 1 children. During these weekly sessions, high calibre musicians from the Prep school perform to our children on a range of instruments, giving them the opportunity to experience the power of live music.
In Year 2 all children begin learning the recorder at the Prep school under the tutelage of the Director of Music and his team.
Pupils have two music lessons per week in Years 3 - 6, at which point the children enter a rotation with ICT which enables them to complete a music project every half term. There is plenty of practical music-making in class, with regular singing and percussion ensembles.
In Years 3 and 4, we explore the instruments of the orchestra, the music of different cultures, and the concept of ‘descriptive’ music, with a particular focus on works such as Prokofiev’s Peter and the Wolf. We begin work on a basic music theory syllabus. Years 5 and 6 are given over to the study of the Baroque and Classical periods. We explore composers such as Bach and Mozart, and the development of the orchestra during these periods. In Years 7 and 8 the focus turns to the Impressionists, film music, the 12-bar blues, and finally to the modern music of bands such as The Beatles.
We also study a separate music technology curriculum, using the music classroom’s suite of iMac computers.
Music
Beyond the Classroom
Most of our music-making is enjoyed outside of classroom lessons. There are two large-scale school concerts per year in the Christmas and Summer terms, two inter-patrol music competitions (for singers and instrumentalists), alongside regular Informal Concerts and recitals featuring the pupils of our peripatetic staff.
We run two orchestras, three choirs, a Big Band and many other chamber ensembles which change from year to year to cater for the needs and talents of the children. These usually include ensembles for our string, brass and wind players, along with our percussionists and rock bands.
Our flagship ensemble is the Chapel Choir, an auditioned group of around 50 children drawn from Years 5-8. The choir regularly leads the worship at the weekly chapel service, and at the school’s Christmas services at Boxgrove Priory. The group enjoys a foreign tour every 1-2 years. Previous destinations include:
Alongside their school commitments, the choir regularly partners the Shopwyke Singers, an adult chamber choir based at the school, in singing well-known choral works.
Individual Music Lessons
We are proud to have a team of over twenty outstanding peripatetic teachers, a number of whom are professional performers. All orchestral instruments are offered, along with piano, drums, guitar (classical and rock), and singing. We are an exam centre for the Associated Board, entering a large number of candidates each term, and our results are consistently high. Pupils are also entered for Trinity music exams, with the drummers and guitarists following their ‘Rock and Pop’ syllabuses.
Music and Drama
Each year the Music and Drama departments combine to produce two large-scale musicals with pupils from Years 6 and 8. Previous Year 6 productions include Rainmaker, Singin' in the Rain, Bugsy Malone, The Lion King, Beauty and the Beast and Joseph. The Year 8 production is produced in just two weeks, after the Common Entrance exams. Previous productions include Mary Poppins, Fiddler on the Roof, The Secret Garden and Little Shop of Horrors. All productions feature a live professional band. There is usually some musical involvement in the productions produced by the Junior Department too. For more information on the various drama productions throughout the year, see the Drama page.
I have been Director of Music at Westbourne House since 1991, having previously enjoyed a freelance career as an organist, and taught at both prep and senior school level. Our ‘music for all’ approach is born out of my belief that every child has musical potential, and it is our aim to provide the stimulus upon which the children can foster a love of music that will last a lifetime.

After School Clubs
Our clubs create opportunities for children to try exciting new things and make friends outside of the classroom.
We have a wide variety of after school clubs from swimming to games design, cooking to football, drama to chess. Please view the current lists of clubs in the Pre-Prep (Reception - Year 2) and Prep School (Year 3 - 8) below.
For busy parents, we also have wraparound care. Learn more about our before and after school care.

pageCache.text:
Childcare
We have a range of childcare options to help busy parents manage their family’s schedules both before and after school as well as extensive after school clubs.
Nursery and Pre-Prep
Morning Club: 7.45 – 8.15am
A very warm welcome and a big smile will greet your child at Morning Club. Your child will be entertained until 8.10am, when he or she will be taken by the hand to their classroom to join his or her teacher and the rest of the class.
A morning session costs £5 and is added to the school bill. Sign up via the Pre-Prep office on 01243 778496.
The Westies Club (after school care): 3.15 – 5.30pm
Children are entertained by Westbourne’s Childcare Supervisor, Emma Eckert, who will collect your child from their classroom at the end of their day and lead them to the Frog Room to receive a healthy snack. Refuelled, there are a range of structured activities on offer for the children to enjoy, which include music and movement, art, construction, baking and a whole host of role-play and games. Children will be given a light supper at 4.45pm.
Sign up online at the beginning of term or get in touch with Katy in the Pre-Prep office. The cost is £8.50 per hour.
If you are collecting children from the Pre-Prep and the Prep School, please collect Nursery and Pre-Prep children first. There will be additional charges for late collection.
Prep School
Breakfast Club: from 7.35am
Prep School pupils can join our boarders for breakfast at 7.35am. The cost for this session is £3.75. Contact the office for further information.
After School Care: until 5.30pm
The Prep School provides a childcare for students in Years 3 and 4 until 5.30pm, except on Saturdays.
Children are entertained by the Year 4 teachers with fun activities in the classroom, sports hall and outside. Sign up by adding your child’s name to the childcare list via the Prep School office. The cost for this session is £8.67. However, if you have an older child (in Years 5 to 8) who you collect at 5.30pm, this session is free of charge.
Please inform the office if you plan to collect your child early from After School Care.

Parent Portal
You can access all the important information about school on our Parent Portal and save it handly to your mobile so you can access it anytime.
Visit www.westbournehouse.org/parent-portal on your mobile.
Pin it! As you arrive at the page on your phone, a pop up will tell you how to add the shortcut to this page to your phone homescreen. However, if you have already dismissed this pop up, here are the instructions:
Android: Tap the menu button and tap Add to homescreen. The icon will appear on your home screen like any other app shortcut or widget, so you can drag it around and put it wherever you like.
iPhone: Tap the Share button on the browser’s toolbar — that’s the rectangle with an arrow pointing upward. It’s on the bar at the bottom of the screen on an iPhone. Tap the Add to Home Screen icon in the Share menu. The shortcut can be dragged around and placed anywhere, including in app folders — just like a normal app icon.
Sports Portal
At the top of the Parent Portal is a link to our Sports Portal. It is worth pinning this to your homescreen as per the instructions above so you can see team lists, read match reports and check where matches are taking place. This information is also available in the Blue Passage.
Integrating the calendar onto your iPhone
Go to calendar from your phone (there's a handy link at the top of the Parent Portal). Click ‘Calendar ICS-ICAL’ and it asks you whether you want to subscribe. Click subscribe and it populates your calendar. You can unsubscribe after from your phone if you wish.

Part-time boarding
“Boarding activities, such as a creative activity involving costume design and performance, further help to enhance pupils’ self-confidence.”
Independent Schools Inspectorate Report, 2025
Part-time boarding is ideal for children who want to stay at school on a regular basis from one to four nights a week. Sometimes this is to enable the child to enjoy the full experience of Westbourne House, sometimes to avoid a daily journey and sometimes simply to fit in with hectic family schedules.
Our boarders reap the benefits: confidence, independence and strong friendships.
We are happy to answer your questions
If you are considering Westbourne House School for your child and have questions about boarding, please contact Aline Pilcher, Head of Admissions, on 01243 530614.
If your child is already at Westbourne House, please contact Peter Fisher, Head of Boarding boarding@westbournehouse.org
Find out about boarding fees.

pageCache.pageTitle: Prep Senior Daily Life | Westbourne House School
pageCache.text:
Prep Senior Daily Life
Hello, my name is Zubin.
I’m in Year 7, and I’m a part-time boarder, boarding on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday nights. On boarding nights, I live in Middle Lodge with other boys in Year 7, as well as our house parents Mr and Mrs Cousens, their baby Phoebe and their dog Truffles. I’ve been at Westbourne House since Year 2. My brother is in Year 5 and my sister is in Year 3.
I boarded last night, so I get a nice lie in! We get up at 7.10am and get ready for the school day, then head to breakfast at 7.30am in the dining room with other boarders and any children who come in early for breakfast. After breakfast we have a bit of free time.
We head to our form rooms. I’m in Mrs Sutcliffe’s form with a group of 20 boys and girls from Years 7 and 8. We get our books ready for the first three lessons, and the register is taken. Mrs Sutcliffe gives us any messages and reminders. We start the day with pastoral time and on Fridays I catch up with my tutor.
We have a set of three lessons. Today we had maths followed by French and ICT. In maths we have been working on transformations, and today we got on to enlargements – which is when a shape gets larger (or smaller), expanding from a centre of enlargement. It reminded me of some of the work we’ve done on perspective in art.
We break for ‘crusts’, which is a funny name for a snack such as bread with jam, butter or marmite, or something like carrots and cucumbers or nachos. We then have break time, when a lot of us rush to the nets to practise batting and bowling. Lots of kids head to the Boundaries (the woods) to make dens or play ‘Family It’.
After break we have two more lessons before lunch. In Geography, we were using some new tools to measure the weather. Mrs Pollock showed us how to measure rainfall with a rain gauge. We are placing these around the grounds and measuring them over a term.
Lunch at school is actually really good. We’ve been working on manners at school this term, so there are funny posters around the dining room reminding us to offer the ketchup to our friends! After lunch we have a pretty long break to play or relax with friends.
I had a short meeting with my personal tutor today. We talked about how I feel about my recent exam results and about how the cricket season is going. I can raise any concerns I have with my tutor – about my school work or anything going on with my friends, but everything is going well at the moment!
We have three lessons after lunch. Each day we have at least one hour playing the great sports we play in the summer term – cricket, athletics and tennis. Cricket is my favourite sport.
We have a short ‘biscuit break’ at 3.30pm, followed by one final lesson in the afternoon at 3.45pm. Today we have Science and we are studying Biology and are doing some dissection.
We have a 45 minute prep session at the end of the day. I can usually finish off my prep during the school day. Today we had Senior Choir - we’re practising for the end of year school concert, where we’re singing a few songs from The Greatest Show together with our awesome Drum Group.
Day pupils go home at 5.30pm, unless they are doing an after school activity like tennis, debate or speech and drama.
We have dinner together in the dining room (except on Wednesdays, when we have a BBQ outside!) and then have free time.
Boarding at Westbourne House is amazing. In the evening we can play outside, use the tennis and squash courts, play table tennis or loads of other options. The house parents arrange fun activities in the evenings, such as slip 'n' slide, water fights and treasure hunts. Sometimes we go out of school to the beach or to the cinema.
We head back to the boarding houses for a shower and some down time in the common room, before lights out at 8.45pm.
Return to read about more children's days.

pageCache.pageTitle: Sport for excellence, sport for all | Westbourne House School
pageCache.text:
Sport for excellence, sport for all
We are passionate about sport and being active. Pupils play a range of sports and all children are encouraged to be their best and to enjoy themselves.
From Year 3, children have the opportunity to play matches at an appropriate level for their current skills and development. It is not just about performance or just about participation. We try to create an environment where both are possible, where sport is accessible to all and everyone is challenged to reach their full potential.
Select an option below
Our nursery children have plenty of space to be active and burn off energy.
We take children outside to our gardens as well as the sports hall to enjoy jumping, jiggling and balancing, football and baby yoga. We start to learn to catch and throw. All the activities centre on boosting children’s coordination, movement memory and their ability to listen to and remember instructions. They are encouraged to enjoy physical activity in a relaxed and secure environment.
In the third term of the final year at nursery, children start weekly swimming lessons in the school pool with our specialist swimming teacher, Mrs Howley. As well as a lot of giggling and splashing, they get used to swimming at school, which prepares them well for their upcoming move into Reception.
Our main goal is develop children’s confidence and instil a love of sport and being active. Each week, children have one session of games (team sports), one session of PE (dance, gym or country dancing) and a swimming lesson. During these sessions, children develop their physical literacy.
We are lucky to be surrounded by lots of space and grass pitches as well as facilities such as the sports hall, dance studio and swimming pool.
By the time your child is ready to move up to Year 3, they will have experienced a number of different sports and activities. These include gymnastics, athletics, dance, ball skills, cricket, rounders and swimming.
Our excellent specialist teachers and coaches encourage enjoyment and passion for sport, as well as pushing pupils to develop flair and intelligent game play. Winning is an aim but we believe matches should be challenging and we work to ensure that match success is not at the cost of some of the important values of sport such as fair play, respect and teamwork.
Being active is healthy for body and mind and has been proven to improve performance in the classroom too. Children enjoy one PE lesson, at least two games lessons and match afternoons. From Year 4 our children take part in structured physical activity sessions every day, often outside in the fresh air. They are running around, having fun, getting fit, and reaping the benefits.
Many of our pupils go on to be awarded sports scholarships, as well as being successful at county, national and international level. We regularly reach the IAPS National Finals in a variety of sports.
Sport for excellence, sport for all
Beyond PE and games lessons
We organise sports tours that reap huge benefits in terms of the children’s skills and playing experience, as well as being a special cultural experience for the children. We have annual trips for senior boys and girls to a variety of destinations such as Barcelona, Netherlands and South Africa and for a variety of sports depending on the preferences of that year group such as football, netball, hockey and cricket.
We organise extensive matches and tournaments against other schools and all ability levels have the opportunity to play competitive sport.
Children enjoy kayaking and canoeing in the pool and on the lake.
There are extensive extra-curricular clubs after school including ballet, football, judo, fencing and gymnastics from their first school year up to Year 8. From Year 3 up, further options are available including golf, athletics, girls’ cricket, tennis, swimming and modern and street dance.
Our boarders also enjoy Real Tennis training and matches after school. Real Tennis is the original racquet sport from which the modern game of tennis derived.
Our sports facilities
Westbourne House School is set in over 100 acres of well-drained playing fields. Our sporting facilities include:
As an Old Westbournian (former pupil), I am especially proud to be the Head of Boys' Sport at Westbourne House!
I am thrilled to share my passion for cricket, squash and hockey - and indeed all sports - with the next generation of pupils.
My goal is simple: to help every pupil, from those who are new to team sports to those who are competing at an elite level outside of school, to develop their skills on and off the field.
Sport and activity is such an important part of people’s lives due to the huge impact it has on physical and mental health. To see children progress and enjoy sport is something I find very satisfying and I simply love our pupils' enthusiasm, engagement and sportsmanship.
My team and I stretch the more experienced athletes while ensuring that all pupils develop their skills and enjoy competitive matches against other teams.
I am a qualified hockey coach, netball coach and umpire. I have also attended CPD in swimming, athletics, cricket, badminton, rounders and climbing. As a teenager I played county hockey and recently I have played county league netball. I would say netball is my passion but I will try my hand at most things!
3 outdoor hard tennis courts
5 outdoor netball courts
2 glass-backed squash courts
25 metre indoor swimming pool
9 hole par 3 golf course
indoor and outdoor cricket nets
dance studio
climbing wall
Christmas and Easter terms
Netball and hockey are the main winter sport for girls. The boys play football, rugby and hockey.
Pupils also take part in cross–country competitions, swimming galas and squash matches. Golf is played throughout the year.
Summer term
The summer term focus for the boys and girls is cricket. Tennis and athletics also feature strongly in this term.
All year groups have one PE lesson a week and pupils love the variety: badminton, basketball, indoor hockey, gymnastics, dance, squash, fitness, swimming, cricket nets, climbing, short tennis, dodgeball, canoeing and kayaking.
In addition, Year 3 has two games lessons per week, Year 4 has three, and Years 5 - 8 have four games lessons every week.
Year 3 pupils play matches on Thursdays, Year 4 on Thursdays and Saturdays and Year 5-8 on Wednesdays and Saturdays.
Our fixture list is appropriate, competitive and aspirational making each season a challenge. We aim for every child to play in at least six matches per term.
In our sports sessions, we aim for the following:
Encourage pupil leadership
Create a safe but challenging environment
Master appropriate techniques and skills
Focus on performance rather than the outcome

pageCache.pageTitle: Community of Parents | Westbourne House School
pageCache.text:
Community of Parents
Before your child starts at Westbourne House, you will receive a year group address list, which gives contact details of all the other families in your child’s year group, so you can see who lives close-by and set up play dates and car sharing. Plus your child’s class representative (a volunteer parent) will give you a call to say hello and welcome you to our parent community.
As well as seeing other parents at drop off and pick up, our parents meet up at school throughout the year for special events such as Mother’s Day celebrations, concerts, performances and class assemblies. In Years 4-8, pupils participate in sports matches on Wednesday afternoons (Year 4, Thursday) and Saturday mornings.
Match days have a wonderful family feel, with parents gathering on the sidelines to cheer and chat, and gathering afterwards over match tea. In the summer term, we encourage families to bring a picnic as described by one of our parents:
Picnic on Saturdays with Zubin and his younger brother Theo and sister Zara, is a great opportunity for us to get together as a family, as often I have not seen the boys since school drop off on Wednesday. We all have a favourite spot that we like to picnic at, usually in clusters of year groups. Usually we host several boys and provide them with a simple sausage roll and snacks. We love catching up with not only our sons but their mates and listen in on their banter which never fails to entertain.

pageCache.pageTitle: Morning Minibus Service | Westbourne House School
pageCache.text:
Morning Minibus Service
Westbourne House offer a morning school transport service from Monday to Friday.
Routes
Based on the interest received from parents, we are running four minibus routes; South Harting, Midhurst, Emsworth and the Witterings.
We have included pick-up points to accommodate as many families as possible whilst trying to keep the time of the journey at a reasonable length.
Midhurst & South Harting
The pick-up points are as follows:
Petworth (as required)Cowdray Farm Shop, MidhurstSouth Harting
The pick-up points are as follows:
East Wittering West Wittering Itchenor Birdham
South Harting, Lavant & Funtington
The pick-up points are as follows:
South HartingThe Earl of March, LavantThe Fox & Hounds, Funtington
Reserve a minibus seat
Please complete the minibus reservation form to reserve your place/s. Seats will be available on a first come, first served basis.
Minibus Reservation Form
Whilst every effort has been made to accommodate as many families as possible, we recognise that some will be disappointed. We ask that you please indicate your interest and location by emailing Rachel at minibus@westbournehouse.org so that your location may be considered in the future.
Fees
The minibus service will be offered at a price of £230 per term per child.
Questions
Please direct any questions to minibus@westbournehouse.org in the first instance.
Additional Information
If your child is under 5 years old, please contact us to discuss before completing a reservation form.
We are using the Westbourne House School minibuses for the morning school pick up service.
The buses are driven by Westbourne House staff.
Whilst every effort is made to ensure the same person drives a route every day, on occasion we will have to use alternative drivers.
We have decided not to include a chaperone, in order to keep costs down for parents.
Families will be billed for the minibus service in arrears.
Running Late or Absent
The minibuses are on a strict timetable to arrive at each pick up spot on time. So as to ensure the children arrive at school on time, the minibuses will not be able to wait for any late arrivals.
If you know you will not be taking the bus one day, we ask that you please send a text message to your driver.
The minibuses park in the Pre-Prep car park. The driver escorts children into the gates, and will escort any Pre-Prep children into the building. The driver will also remind children to take all their belongings, and will assist with any big bags or instruments.

Personal Tours and Visits
Personal Tours
We would be delighted to arrange a tour for you. You can visit the Nursery, Pre-Prep and Prep School during the school week. If you are specifically looking at the Prep School, you can also choose to visit on a Saturday morning when you would see our matches and optional Saturday activities.
To book, fill out the form below and our Admissions team will be in touch.
Getting to know the school
If your child has a particular interest, such as drama or music, your family would be very welcome to come to one of our school shows or concerts. Please contact admissions@westbournehouse.org to organise.
